text: By midday, the heat climbed into the sky like flame off dry wood.
Leuk swung his short-handled hoe with rhythmic precision, turning over the rich earth furrow by furrow.
But Bouki leaned against his hoe, mopping his forehead with a leafy branch.
'Ah, Leuk,' Bouki groaned, clutching his side with exaggerated sorrow, 'a sudden fever has seized my bones!
My head spins like a top.
I must rest under the shade of the baobab for just a little while, or I shall surely perish.'
Leuk smiled knowingly, his paws never pausing.
'The hoe does not ask who watches, only who digs.'
